newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes down, watching West African arb.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes down, watching West African arb.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were slightly lower on Monday with players assessing the arbitrage opportunities for West African crude.
The January Brent/Dubai -- the most active in Asia -- was assessed at $1.90/$1.95 per barrel, in slightly from $1.91/$1.97 on Friday but continuing the narrowing trend of recent sessions.
But traders said the spread was still too wide to clearly say the arbitrage window for West African crudes was open.
Market sources said China's Sinochem was checking the economics of importing Cabinda, which represented the best value, but nothing had been fixed yet.
Paper Tapis levels came off 40 cents on November, to be bid around $23.50 per barrel, partly catching up with recent Brent losses.
December Brent on Friday fell 17 cents to $22.50 and on Monday in early London had regained 14 cents of the losses.
Dubai intermonth spreads were mostly steady around 45 cents, in line with the recent market and five trades on Friday in Jan/Feb, Feb/Mar and Mar/Apr, all at 45 cents.
Traders said the wet market was extremely quiet as players started to prepare for the next trading month of January for Gulf grades and December for regional grades.

The official selling price for October Oman crude was raised to $22.50 per barrel but the differential to published Dubai quotes came in to 74 cents per barrel from 78 cents, which traders said was in line with expectations.
Traders were waiting late on Monday for the release of official selling prices of other Gulf grades.
